canonical_claim: Cache insertion captures a local sequence before loading and publishes the view only when that sequence is unchanged, preventing a stale in-flight read from repopulating after a local write.
The cache mutex must not be held during `resolveRef`, `readManifest`, `HEAD`, `GET`, or decode, and single-flight must be scoped per `(namespace, ref)` or `ManifestId` rather than globally.

CAS blob content hashes use CityHash128 consistently with MergeTree file checksums, while tree or manifest identity also uses CityHash128 where other higher-level identities commonly use SipHash128; the review recommends documenting or revisiting that choice under the collision model.
RunFile block and footer CRC32C should remain until RunRef.checksum is either verified as a full-run artifact hash before trust or removed or demoted before release

CAS fsck classifies canonical physical keys absent from the catalog at a post-listing observation cut as soft FsckClass::JanitorPending, with report fields namespace_janitor_pending, namespace_janitor_pending_bytes, and namespace_janitor_pending_lives; these fields are excluded from kFsckHardFindings.; Canonical catalog-absent objects are inert debris that must never damage data; fsck therefore needs a grammar-discriminated `janitor_pending` class rather than treating all such debris as a hard corruption finding.

CasFsck.cpp uses observe-then-cut classification: it buffers canonical candidates during the physical LIST, reads a fresh catalog cut after listing completes, and classifies candidates against that cut to protect concurrent namespace creation.

The anomaly and carried-hold terms in `suppress_destructive` are structural defense-in-depth: in current in-fold paths they co-fire with frontier incompleteness and cannot be isolated by the existing test seams.
`RefPlan` has a private mandatory constructor, is non-assignable, exposes const views only, and has neither mutable `foldState` nor a destructive `releaseFoldStates` operation.
Raw `RoundInput` construction is private to `Gc` and the narrow named `tests::buildRefWalkPlanForTest` wrapper, preventing arbitrary scan/catalog pairs from bypassing the production binding boundary.

The authoritative `CaRefLaneCore` model composes the existing single six-state append lane with a bounded identity/cache submodel containing two runtime ids, two durable life ids, one non-authoritative name slot, one old handle, immutable identity records, per-runtime cache/durable markers, one delayed-invalidation target, and fence state.
An already-issued stale request may land only while its adopted proof remains current; the B-drained takeover trace is a helping barrier rather than atomic revocation of an independent catalog CAS.
The copy `const RefTableState before = state;` in `E3AdmitsPreviewLeavesStateByteIdentical` must remain an independent snapshot because `state` is mutated later for byte-identical comparison.

The TLA+ model collapses the real `armMountFence .. noteRemounted` interval into one atomic reclaim action because the op gate refuses durable admission while the state is not `Live` and older fence generations fail revalidation.

On existing non-CAS disks, immediate local-filesystem visibility and object-storage parts represented as independent files generally prevented the weak disk-transaction contract from causing direct data loss, but MergeTree still depended on implementation-specific visibility and early sub-part commits.

CAS's documented deployment rule from the security audit: never share a CAS pool across trust domains until SEC-1 (collision poisoning), SEC-2 (dedup existence oracle), and SEC-3 (no intra-pool authorization) are addressed; the single highest-leverage code fix common to both the Jepsen-style consistency audit and the security audit is a `writer_epoch`-fenced shard CAS precondition, which simultaneously closes SEC-7 (NTP/pause-amplifiable fencing) and the J1/J2/J3 split-brain class.
The TXN-final phase-3 soak completed with `dangling=0`, recovered from five faults and three restarts, reported `ABORTED-retried INSERT=0`, and drained the pool to 256 bytes.
The S38 late-PUT fence test passed 19 of 19 verdicts and the real object store returned HTTP 412 for a straggler's conditional create at a sealed id.
`CaB140DangleMerge` passed its empty-`Trees` configuration `m_empty_trees.cfg` as green.
`CaIncarnationCore_empty_hashes.cfg` passed as green with `Hashes = {}`.

In the observed list-incompleteness occurrence, ref-log objects `0x1430c`, `0x1430d`, and `0x1430e` were uploaded in strict ID order at 16:47:19.211480, 16:47:19.212340, and 16:47:19.213680 respectively.
The first walk returned ref-log object `0x1430e` after its upload, but did not return the two earlier objects `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` even though they had been durable for 1.3–2.2 ms at that point.
A measurement of 65,263 ref-log uploads found zero out-of-order uploads after partitioning by writer epoch.
For the observed disagreement, `ch2` deleted zero ref objects over all time, `ch1` deleted zero ref objects during 16:47:00–16:48:00, and `ch2` deleted zero ref objects during that interval.
Relaxing the condemned-token gate for non-pending entries was rejected because `SabotageAdoptRetiredToken` demonstrates that binding a listed token is unsafe.
Accepting a condemned token without resurrecting it is unsound because exact-token GC deletion can graduate and delete that incarnation, leaving the committed manifest dangling.

Skipping the occupancy `HEAD` on a dedup-cache hit is unsafe: the cached matching blob may have had zero in-degree and been fully deleted since caching, and after the proposed §5 change an absent `.meta` object would look like Clean, so only `HEAD` or a body GET can distinguish absence from a live blob.
A fallback is acceptable only when uncertainty concerns the mechanism; uncertainty about the source must abort and retry rather than silently taking another route to the same peer.
CAS code uses `LOGICAL_ERROR` only for genuine programming invariants and uses `CORRUPTED_DATA`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, or `ABORTED` for the corresponding existing CAS error classes.

The primary soak correctness oracle is all-replica agreement on `count() + sum(sipHash64(*))`, with an absolute Python-side prediction for deterministic `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM numbers(N)` workloads.

Backend conformance table: AWS S3 (versioning off) uses ETag, fully conforming, validated live 2026-07-03, probe-gated at startup (DeleteObject If-Match GA'd Sep 2025). RustFS 1.0.0-beta.8 uses ETag, empirically verified 2026-06-11, leading open-source CI candidate, with known issue rustfs#3231 (overwrite-leak of objects above the store's inline threshold, e.g. 128 KiB, in unversioned buckets) that can produce metacache LIST storms and false 404s on HEAD -- the only source of GC fold clamps observed to date. Azure Blob uses ETag (write-sensitive), supported and probe-gated, with versioning/soft-delete required off. GCS uses generation, binding specified but implementation deferred, fail-closed until probed. MinIO OSS (archived 2026-02) has If-Match on DELETE silently ignored (confirmed 2026-06-11) -- fail-closed. Ceph RGW has no conditional delete documented -- fail-closed.
